Subject: Questions on DPA language: onshore fallback & temporary analytics vendor

Hi Neha / Laura,

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft last week. Our legal team finished an initial pass and had two items we'd like to confirm before we loop procurement:

1) Onshore fallback: the Clarion privacy team needs explicit operational evidence that in the event of offshore subprocessor outage/availability issues, data processing for US residents can be routed or degraded to onshore capacity within a defined SLA window. Can you point us to the concrete controls/metrics Redwood is willing to contractually commit to or provide an alternatives clause?

2) Temporary analytics subprocessor: BrightAnalytics (Ben Carter copied) will be engaged for a 12-week pilot to run aggregated usage analytics on query telemetry. We need to confirm this vendor will only receive pseudonymized aggregates, retention capped to 90 days, and that Redwood will act as the controller/processor mapping per your DPA (i.e., is this a service provider/subprocessor relationship or something else you consider a sale?).

Attached is a checklist our counsel uses — we flagged the sections where we need your input. Can you also attach any subprocessor evidence (SOC2 or equivalent) for transient analytics providers and the suggested onshore fallback runbook?

Best,
Maya
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Clarion Health

Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on DPA language: onshore fallback & temporary analytics vendor

Maya — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, then answers and attachments:

Summary: Redwood can accept clarifying DPA language that treats BrightAnalytics as a subprocessor (service provider) with constraints on telemetry access (pseudonymized aggregates only), a 90-day retention cap, and no sale of data. For the onshore fallback ask, we can commit to an operational SLA for activation of onshore fallback within 24 hours of verified outage for Tier-1 anomalies and provide runbook evidence and test logs quarterly as contract exhibits. See attached redline and subprocessor matrix.

Details:
- Subprocessor classification: We consider BrightAnalytics a subprocessor (service provider) when contracted by Clarion through Redwood. We will amend the DPA Section 3(c) to add explicit language: "Temporary analytics subprocessors engaged for pilots are bound by the same limitations on use (no sale, no re-identification) and retention as permanent subprocessors; any deviation requires prior written consent."

- Pseudonymization: telemetry sent to BrightAnalytics will be pre-aggregated and pseudonymized at Redwood's edge. No raw prompt/response strings leave the environment. We'll include the aggregation thresholds in the redline.

- Retention: A contractual cap of 90 days for pilot telemetry, with automated deletion procedure documented in the runbook (attached).

- Onshore fallback: Our proposed contractual language is to commit to activation of onshore capacity within 24 hours of an outage determination for Tier-1 incidents, with a target RTO of 24 hours and a communication timeline. Operational evidence we can include as exhibits: prior quarterly failover test logs, onshore capacity reservation certificates (for Dedicated customers), and a runbook snippet that spells out the steps. Note: SLA-backed dedicated pools are a paid option; the DPA will include an appendix describing the different remedies / credits where a customer leverages Dedicated.

I've attached: redwood-dpa-proposed-redline.docx, subprocessor-matrix-clarion.csv, transit-encryption-diagram.png. Aditya — can you confirm the technical description of pseudonymization and that no KV cache snapshots are part of the telemetry export?

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
